Advanced scientific toolsLaboratory import, reference grids, scientific review and additional nutrient models

Import laboratory analysis

Use a long-format lab CSV with one row per ingredient × analyte. Report dry_matter first as percent of as-fed mass, then other analytes with their explicit basis (% / g/kg / mg/kg, or MJ/kg / kcal/kg for energy). Each row needs a sample date, lab/method, evidence ID and use-rights category. Conversions are checked and original values are retained in the editable JSON record. No published database values are bundled.

A laboratory import replaces the ingredient table and never fills unreported nutrients with zero. You must still supply your own local prices and inclusion bounds.

Scientific and safety checklist

Each ingredient has a new hazard/suitability screening field and document identifier in its table row. Mark a pass only if you have supporting test results and local species-specific checks. This preflight identifies known gaps but does not certify animal nutrition or regulatory compliance. Calculations remain usable while feeding/manufacturing release stays separate.

No scientific readiness check run yet.

Reference-based nutrient target estimator

Reference grids contain no bundled numerical anchors. Generate nutrient targets by interpolating documented, species/stage-specific reference points. Enter measurements for the animal, import a licensed reference grid, or create/edit your own. This interpolator never extrapolates beyond measured reference anchors; it does not predict feed intake or replace independent nutritional review.

This species/stage still requires manually entered targets. Automatic interpolation is being developed for additional stages.

The stage template represents only eight selected constraints. Interpolated concentrations are not a complete diet requirement model; true adequacy also needs intake, micronutrients, digestibility, hazards, regulations and independent review. Claims entered in a local browser are not verified authentication.

Historical poultry reference preview

Try selected values from a 2020 USDA NRCS poultry technical note, itself based on older NRC 1994 recommendations. The historical reference is included to demonstrate transparent sourcing, conversion and gap analysis, not as a modern commercial diet prescription. Commercial rights for the underlying adapted NRC data have not been cleared.

Only broiler starter/grower/finisher and laying-hen historical examples are preloaded. All other animal/stage requirements remain blank rather than inheriting unrelated species numbers. Missing energy, digestible amino acids, micronutrients and real feed-safety checks must be addressed by a qualified professional. Source values apply to a 90% DM diet and are converted to a DM basis before comparison.

Nutrient profile review records

Create an editable review dossier for each animal and stage. Audit the eight nutrient targets for exact stage match, units, documentary rights, reviewer claims, and outstanding feed-safety checks. This is not a professional review or approval service: no credentials, signatures, permissions or completeness are authenticated here.

Additional scientific and release-evidence checks

A completed audit means only that the entered evidence fields pass structural checks. The 8 selected constraints are not a complete nutrient, safety or intake model. Data is handled locally in your browser. For regulatory use, implement server-side identity, signature, independent review, audit and licensing verification.

THE EXPERIENCE BEHIND RATIONWISE

Practical feeding science, grounded in farmers’ realities.

Dr. Surya Bahadur Singh is an animal nutrition specialist whose career spans research, university teaching, feed manufacturing and livestock development. He completed postgraduate studies in animal nutrition and doctoral research at the University of Aberdeen, Scotland.

At Nepal’s Cattle Feed and Carcass Utilization Project in Hetauda, he developed and balanced rations for dairy cattle, broilers, laying hens and pigs while strengthening feed-ingredient inspection and quality control. As a consultant to Everest Feed Industries, he developed stage-specific broiler and layer feeds, including formulations for different commercial poultry strains.

He taught applied animal nutrition at the Institute of Agriculture and Animal Sciences in Rampur, prepared practical nutrition manuals, and helped livestock officers and farmers apply least-cost ration formulation. His advisory work has also supported livestock and rural-development initiatives in Nepal and other South Asian countries.

Feed formulationDairy cattle, poultry and pigs
Feed qualityIngredient assessment and mill practices
Teaching & advisoryNutrition education and farmer-focused tools

Profile adapted from Dr. Singh’s autobiography, From Open Skies to Distant Horizons: A Discourse with Destiny, particularly the chapters on Aberdeen, the Hetauda feed project, feed-industry consulting, and his teaching and publications.
